name: Net Naming Linter
blurb: checks net names against a convention and lists the inconsistent ones
intro: Paste net names (one per line) or a KiCad .net netlist. It checks case, separators, illegal characters, voltage style (3V3 vs 3.3V), active-low style (nRESET, RESET_N, RESET#, ~{RESET}), differential-pair suffixes and partners, bus index style and names that split one net two ways, and suggests renames.

inputs.label: Net names
inputs.placeholder: one net per line, or paste a KiCad .net file
inputs.default:
GND
+3V3
+3.3V
VCC_5V
5V0

BOOT0

spi1_sck
SPI1_CS_N
I2C SDA
I2C_SCL
USB_D+
USB_D-
ETH_TX_P
ETH_TX_N

DATA[0]
DATA1
nIRQ

inputs.label: Max name length
inputs.help: Some CAM and simulation tools truncate long names.

DATA[0]

usage: Give the net names as text, one per line (a CSV/TSV first column or a KiCad .net netlist also works), and the convention: case (auto, upper, lower), active-low style (auto, n, _N, #, ~{}), voltage style (auto, V for 3V3, dot for 3.3V) and a maximum length. It returns counts, a table of each inconsistent net with the problem and a suggested name, and a Renames text (old -> new). Use it during schematic review before layout or before exporting a netlist.
sources: Rule of thumb: common schematic-review conventions (IPC-2612-1 style consistent naming, vendor reference designs)
Voltage R-notation (3V3) after IEC 60062 value coding; KiCad netlist S-expression format for parsing
